messages:
arjun: FYI hit a weird customer repro where the client disconnects during streaming, then our edge tries to reroute to a different upstream while teardown is still in flight. results: duplicate responses + missing trailers. logs below:

arjun: ```
edge: conn=abc123 state=teardown->draining
upstream: resp=200 stream=partial trailer=error-code:42
edge: route_change triggered by healthcheck, new upstream attached
client: RST_STREAM
edge: second upstream returns partial as well -> client sees duplicates
```

maya: yikes. do we have headers we can attach to make reroute noop if teardown started? like a teardown-idempotency token?

arjun: we have request-id but it's not tied to stream-teardown state. once edge detaches session it treats as new request.

sophia: two main risks: 1) duplicate side-effects if upstreams commit (eg: event emission) 2) binary payloads/trailers getting lost on mid-reroute. preserving trailers is hard if we short-circuit.

lee: short term: prevent route swap during teardown window. patch: when edge sees FIN from upstream or client-initiated RST, mark session "tearing_down" for 100ms and reject route updates. cheap and backwards compatible.

maya: 100ms sounds arbitrary. can we make it workload-aware? eg: if response contains Transfer-Encoding: chunked or streaming, extend window to 500ms. otherwise 100ms.

arjun: that helps but still racy for slow upstreams. also hurts bursty healthchecks that flip a node quickly.

sophia: alternative: handshake ACK from upstream for final trailer delivery. proto: when upstream sends last-chunk/trailer, it must also send a teardown-token header which edge will ACK back to upstream. only after ACK is route-change-safe. that guarantees trailers won't be lost.

lee: handshake needs to be lightweight. we can piggyback on existing control frames. but we'd need upstream adapters for non-redwood models.

maya: we could do a hybrid: default conservative timer + opt-in teardown-ack header for services that can support it. default timer protects most; opt-in gives correctness for those that need trailers.

arjun: agree. ops concern: what about long-poll websockets / long streaming endpoints? timers are bad there. must rely on opt-in headers.

sophia: also need idempotency for side-effects. recommend adding an "edge-teardown-id" header generated by edge at request start and passed upstream. upstreams can use it to de-dup commits.

lee: summary of proposal: 1) add edge-teardown-id header at request start (opt-in enforcement via config) 2) implement conservative teardown-window (100ms normal, 500ms for streaming) 3) support optional teardown-ack handshake header to block reroute until ACKed 4) document upstream adapter requirements for non-redwood runtimes.

maya: can we avoid breaking TLS termination assumptions? these headers live between edge and upstreams (not visible to clients). we need config knobs for Dedicated/Private where customers manage upstreams.

arjun: yep headers internal only. for Private, put it behind a feature flag until we validate with onprem kit.

ops-bot: deploy-notes: will require edge runtime + gateway config change. plan gate: canary on non-prod clusters, then staging 24h, then prod. alert on increased 5xx or duplicate-event metrics.

sophia: follow-up RFC items: - wire format for teardown-ack - idempotency semantics and recommended upstream behavior - config defaults per deployment type - perf impact tests (heap/latency)

lee: I'll prototype timer+flag quick patch for ingress-gateway. if we can get teardown-id header generation in, we can run a replay test to detect duplicate commits.

maya: thanks. can we add a short test plan: 1) replay recorded streaming session with mid-teardown reroute 2) validate trailers preserved with teardown-ack 3) validate no duplicate side-effects when upstreams respect edge-teardown-id

arjun: added to my backlog. will open a follow-up RFC/PR with specifics and sample header names.

maya: :thumbsup: let's also thread this into infra-oncall so routing/healthcheck folks are aware.

lee: pinging infra team next. will CC ops and product if any compatibility concerns.
